newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to announce employment plans on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to announce employment plans on Thursday.

text.p: South African Labour Minister Tito Mboweni will on Thursday announce the cabinet's decision on planned employment legislation which has split business and labour, his office said.

Mboweni will address a news conference in Johannesburg which was expected to start at around 10 a.m. (0800 GMT) on Thursday, spokeswoman Estelle Randall told Reuters. Cabinet meets on Wednesday to discuss the pending legislation.
Employers, who fear the legislation will increase its costs, object to a proposed reduction in maximum working hours to 45 from 46 and subsequently to 40 hours over five years.

Other proposals expected include an increase in annual paid leave from two to three weeks a year and maternity leave from three months to four months, as well as raising the overtime premium from time and a third to time and a half.
Two major concerns for employers are the increased unit labour costs and limited labour market flexibility implied by the bill.

The Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu), which generally favours the proposals, said earlier on Tuesday its leadership would react on Friday, once they had had a chance to assess the cabinet's decision and any changes which could be made.

Cosatu, an alliance partner of the ruling African National Congress and the largest union federation in the country, is mobilising for a one-day strike on May 12 to ensure key elements of the Employment Standards Bill are not watered down.

Labour, business and government have been in talks in the labour market chamber of the National Economic Development and Labour Council (Nedlac) on the new employment standards law since early last year but have so far failed to reach agreement.
